claims.text: The initial nanoparticles are an equimolar Ni-Co-Fe-Cr-Mn alloy synthesized as a single-phase solid solution.
Low-level Al doping can minimally perturb the bulk equimolar composition while enabling Al surface segregation.
During high-temperature exposure, doped Al preferentially migrates to the nanoparticle surface.
Surface-segregated Al reacts with available oxygen to form an ultra-thin Al2O3 layer.
The resulting Al2O3 layer is passivating and protective.
The Al2O3 surface layer retards atomic diffusion and elemental segregation.
The passivating layer lowers surface energy.
Lowering surface energy reduces the driving force for further diffusion and phase separation.
Suppressing diffusion and phase separation helps maintain the homogeneous solid-solution phase.
Al-doped nanoparticles will show less elemental segregation than undoped nanoparticles under oxidizing thermal cycling.
Al-doped nanoparticles will retain a more uniform phase than undoped nanoparticles under oxidizing thermal cycling.
The protective effect of Al doping will be minimal under inert conditions because oxidation is limited.
Under inert conditions, Al-doped particles may behave similarly to the undoped baseline.
Stabilization requires an Al concentration sufficient for surface passivation but low enough not to compromise bulk phase homogeneity.
The stabilization effect should be strongest when oxygen is available to form Al2O3.
The controlled comparison uses Al-doped and undoped Ni-Co-Fe-Cr-Mn nanoparticles subjected to identical thermal cycling from 473 K to 1923 K in oxidizing and inert atmospheres.
TEM, EDS, and XPS can be used to assess morphology or phase boundaries, elemental segregation, and surface Al2O3, respectively.
Failure of Al doping to produce a statistically significant reduction in segregation or phase separation under oxidizing conditions would falsify the predicted stabilization.
Comparable stabilization under inert conditions where Al2O3 formation is suppressed would falsify attribution of stabilization to Al2O3 passivation.
